64859.subject: Geography
64859.question_text:
(a) List two examples of volcanic mountains in the world.
(b) With the aid of annotated diagram, describe how composite cones are formed.
(c) Outline three causes of landslides.
64859.explanation:
(a) Examples of Volcanic Mountains in the World:- -Mount Kilimanjaro in Tanzania -Mount Vesuvius in Italy - Mount Stromboli in Italy -Mount Etna in Italy -Mount Popocatepetl in Mexico -Mount Mayon in Philippines Mount Pinatubo in Philippines -Mount Cameroun in Cameroun -Mount Cotopaxi in Ecuador -Mount Fuji in Japan - Mount Krakatoa in Indonesia Kenya Chimborazo in Ecuador -Mount Kenya in -Mount -Mount Merapi in Sumatra - mount chimborazo in Ecuador-Mount Elgon in New Zealand-Mount Ararat in Turkey -Mount Elbruz in Russia -Mount Pelee in West Indies -Mount paracutin in Mexico-Vulcan de Fuego in Gautemala -Mount St. Helena in USA -Mount Tambora in Indonesia

(b) Description of How Composite cones are Formed:--Formed due to tectonic activity -Formed from several eruptions -Begin with violent and explosive eruptions-Materials are thrown very high into the atmosphere -Ash and cinder materials -Fall back to build a cone and cinder around the vent -Accumulation of ash and cinder around the vent -Eruption ceases and is followed by lava flow-Lava pours out to settle on top of the existing Layers of materials -The materials form a cone -The cone keeps increasing in height and girth with more eruptions Subsequent violent explosions create cracks along the flanks or sides -Subsidiary conduits or pipes develop at the sides of the main cone -Lava passes through the cracks/pipes, cools and solidifies -Leading to the formation of dykes - This process leads to the formation of subsidiary parasitic cones or cone lets -Crater forms at the peak of the cone -At times the whole top of the volcano blows off or sinks -This forms a huge crater called caldera.


(c) Causes of Landslide:--Prolonged heavy rainfall -Undercutting of slopes by streams and waves-Earthquake and volcanic activities -Construction of roads-Farming along slopes -Quarrying and mining along steep slopes -Animal trampling on overlying rocks -Force of gravity -Dissolution of carbonate materials by water-River incision undermines slope stability- Wave actions along the coast -Deforestation-Lubricating action of rain water-Regolith rich in clay (rock structure).

64866.subject: Geography
64866.question_text:
(a) Name three processes of wind transportation in an arid region.
(b) With the aid of a diagram, describe the characteristics and mode of formation of a deflation hollow.
64866.explanation:
(a) Processes of wind Transportation in an Arid Region:- -Suspension -Traction/surface creep-Saltation.

(b) Characteristics and Mode of Formation of a Deflation Hollow: - Characteristics:--A wind erosional feature

-Found in desert areas -Depression in the desert-Has gentle slides-It is deep -Floor at times reaches the water table -Water sometimes collects in it to form oasis-May have luxuriant vegetation along its sides - Surface is of fine debris (clay or silt) -Surface could be of evaporite (sodium chloride or sodium carbonate) -Ranges in size from few square metres to hundreds of square kilometres-Some are of Quaternary age -Called playas/pans/flats/dayas/ deflation basins/blow outs -Habitable when occupied by oasis-Examples are the Qattara depression in Egypt, Tovat, Toaodeni, El Golea, Jalo, Dakhla, Al-Kufrah, Fayum in Egypt.

Mode of Formation:- -Formed in desert areas -Vegetation cover should be absent- Surface soil should be soft and jointed -Wind deflation process sets in - the softer materials are blown out -Continuous wind action -Eddy action sets in -Depression is created -Floor may reach the water table -Water collects to form a lake or an oasis -At times faulting occurs in less resistant rocks-The area is then affected by deflation -Eddy action aids to create a hollow.

64870.subject: Geography
64870.question_text:
(a) Explain four reasons for which temperature decreases with height within the troposphere.
(b) With the aid of a diagram, describe the mode of formation of orographic rainfall.
64870.explanation:
(a) Reasons for which Temperature Decreases with Height Within the Troposphere: -Air is not heated directly by the sun's rays -Rays strike the earth's surface and heat it first -Air receives its heat from the heat absorbed by the earth's surface -Through the processes of conduction and convection-Since the earth surface is heated first, places closer to the earth experience high temperature -Temperature decreases with height -The rate of decrease is known as environmental lapse rate -Which is 6.5°C for every 1000m of ascent -When unsaturated air mass ascends vertically, it expands and cools adiabatically -Air receives heat from CO,, S0, and aerosols which are more concentrated near the surface -  Air density is more at the base and as such holds more heat than the scanty air molecules at higher altitude.

(b)

Description of the Mode of Formation of Orographic Rainfall:--Also called relief rainfall -Air absorbs water as it flows over land and water bodies -Relief rainfall develops in highland areas -Air comes into contact with a barrier such as mountain-Air is forced to rise or ascend -As it rises, it is Cooled by expansion in the higher altitudes due to decrease in atmospheric pressure -Further ascent cools the air until it is saturated at dew point-Condensation takes place-Clouds are formed -Further cooling of the 'clouds leads to rain formation-Rain falls on the windward slope as relief rainfall -Dry descending wind at the leeward slope brings little or no rainfall.

64874.subject: Geography
64874.question_text:
(a) What is volcanic intrusion ?
(b) Describe the characteristics and mode of formation of a block mountain.
(c) List three landforms that are associated with intrusive volcanic activities.
64874.explanation:
(a) Meaning of Volcanic Intrusion:  Volcanic intrusion occurs when the magma cools and solidifies within the earth's crust..

(b) Characteristics and Mode of Formation of a Block Mountain: Also called a. horst - occurs mostly in areas of intensive tectonic activities-Surface could.be flat -surface could be slightly tilted- Made of hard rocks-Modest In size -Steep-sided- Devoid of peaks -Can become irregular due to erosion and action of rivers -Bordered by, two parallel faults - Bordered by lowlands -Lowlands can be basins or rift valleys- Stand out above/the general level -Examples are Black Forest and Vosges in France, Harz mountain in Germany, Ruwenzori Mountain in Uganda, Hunsruck Mountain in Germany, etc.
Mode of Formation:- -Formed in areas of intensive tectonic activities -Earth movements bring about cracks/faults - Cracks/faults may be more than one -Crusted layer is broken into blocks- cracks/ faults can develop in parallel forms- If faults are of normal types-Tensional forces set in -May result in the central part standing while the flanks' pull apart and subside -This leaves behind the central blocks standing as block mountain-Alternatively when the faults are of reverse or thrust types -Compressional forces may set in -they, force the flanks over the central block- the central block subsides to form a rift valley- The flanks rise to form block mountains.

(c) Landforms that are Associated with Intrusive Volcanic Activities:-Dykes-Sill -Laccolith -Phacolith -Lopolith -Batholiths -Stock or bosses.

64892.subject: Geography
64892.question_text:
(a) List: (i) three factors that influence weathering; (ii) two effects of landslides.
(b) Describe the following processes of weathering: (i) exfoliation; (ii) frost action.
64892.explanation:
(a)(i) Factors that Influence Weathering:- -Climate -Rock structure-Vegetation -Topography/relief - Time -Animals (ii) Effects of Landslide:--Loss of human life -Debris can block streams, or rivers to form a temporal lake Destruction of properties -Displacement of people - Silting of rivers and lakes -Destruction of settlements-Destruction of farmlands-Renders an area vulnerable to soil erosion -The debris can block highways and railway lines.

(b) Description of Processes of Weathering:- (i) Exfoliation:- A form of mechanical or physical weathering-Takes place in arid and semi-arid regions -there is a big difference between daytime and nighttime temperatures  -As the rocks are heated in the daytime, the outer layers expand - expansion is more on the surface than in the interior - As it cools in the night it contracts - Contraction is more on the surface than in the interior - Continuous expansion and contraction produce stress on the outermost layer- the outer layer pulls away -The outer layer peels off from the cooler interior -in a process called exfoliation - the peeling resembles that of onion peels-the boulder left behind after the peeling is called exfoliation domes - Could also be as a result of unloading of over-burden or pressure release -This occurs mainly in the Tropics -Plutonic rocks are under pressure-- the rocks are compressed by overburden -When exposed by erosion- the pressure on them is released -The rocks expand slightly in volume - the expansion causes the surtace layer to crack and peel off-The rock peels are thin and parallel to the rock surface-The onion-like peels called "sheet structire" -exfoliation dome is left behind.
(ii) Frost action: A form of mechanical or physical weathering -Also called frost wedging-Takes place in mid-latitude and temperate regions-Can also occur in mountainous regions - such areas are subject to freezing -Cracks and crevices need to develop on rocks -Water in the form of rainfall or snow seeps into the cracks-the water freezes -Water increases in size when it freezes-Water increases by 10% when frozen -The frozen water exerts pressure on the walls of the rock -The pressure widens the cracks -In the day or summer, ice melts and Water seeps deeper into the widened cracks -the process of freeze and thaw continues -This eventually lead to the shattering of rocks into blocks in a process called frost action -Angular rock fragments accumulate -Called talus and Screes.

64896.subject: Geography
64896.question_text:
(a) Define the term ecosystem.
(b) Describe the main components of the ecosystem citing two examples of each.
(c) Explain two ways in which the components of the ecosystem are interdependent.
64896.explanation:
(a) Definition of the Term Ecosystem: It is the interaction between and among, living organisms and their physical environment (or non-living things) 

(b) Main Components of the Ecosystem and their Examples: Abiotic:-the non-living component or the physical component-examples of the abiotic component are soil, water, gases, sunlight, etc 
Biotic:-the living or biological component -examples of the biotic component are animals, plants, saprophytes, birds, parasites, fish, etc. 
(c) Ways in which the Components of the Ecosystem are Interdependent: Water cycle illustrates the interdependence between the components -Carbon cycle illustrates the interdependence between the components- Nitrogen cycle illustrates the interdependence between. the components -All human activities are mainly carried out on land -Humans return to the land/soil after death -Soil provides habitat for living organisms-When organisms die, they enrich the soil-Food produced by the use of sunlight and water are taken by animals-Animals die to return humus to the abiotic component-Animals draw oxygen from abiotic components and release carbon dioxide to plants which utilize the carbon dioxide and release oxygen back to the abiotic.
